transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. Well, I came in because I just feel like... I've got this motor running inside me all day long. If I have to sit still for a bit, like at church, or out in the clinic waiting room, or even just at home, I start feeling trapped. I just have to get up or do something.
Would you say you've felt this restless, need-to-move feeling since you were a kid, or is this something that started more recently as an adult?

It's been like this since I was a kid. I remember, back when I was a boy in school... teachers were always moving my seat around because I just could not stay put. I talked out of turn a lot, and I always got in trouble for jumping up before class was even done. So, yeah, it's definitely not a new thing for me.

When you feel this urge to get up and move, is it usually accompanied by worrying thoughts or a sense of dread, or does it feel more like a physical restlessness without particular worries attached to it?

No, it's not really a worry thing. I don't have any dread or bad thoughts like that when it happens. It's just... physical, I guess. Like my body just needs to go. My mind isn't stuck on worrying about anything, it's just that I physically can't stay in one spot.
Aside from the restlessness, do you also struggle with staying focused on tasks, forgetting things, or losing track of details, especially when something isn't very stimulating?

Yeah, I do struggle with that. Like... when folks are talking through ride times, or giving me pantry lists, or even going over church plans. I listen good at first, I really do. But then... my mind just slips off somewhere else. And before I know it, I realize I missed the pieces I really needed to hear. So, yeah, staying focused on stuff like that is pretty tough for me.
Do you often find yourself interrupting conversations, blurting out answers before someone finishes a question, or having trouble waiting your turn in line or in discussions?

Yeah, I do that a lot. It's like... I just jump right in. I'll blurt out an answer before the pastor, or my cousin, or even the lady at the food pantry is even done talking. And then half the time, I realize I answered the wrong thing because I didn't wait to hear the whole question. Or I just end up making them mad because I cut them off. It's hard for me to just wait.

Would you say these problems with focus, restlessness, and impulsivity have caused real difficulties for you in more than one area of your life—like at work, at home, and in your relationships—rather than just being an occasional annoyance?

Yeah, it's definitely a lot more than just an annoyance. It's... it's caused real problems for me everywhere. 

People at the church, the folks at the food pantry, and even my own family—they've pretty much stopped trusting me with things. Like, they won't trust me with giving rides, keeping track of appointments, or handling supplies anymore because of how I am. It's hard because... well, I feel like I just keep letting everybody down, even when I really mean to help them out.
Do you drink a lot of caffeine, use any recreational drugs or stimulants, or have any medical conditions like thyroid problems that might explain this restlessness and trouble focusing?

No, sir. I don't really drink much coffee or anything like that. Just water, mostly. And I don't mess with any drugs or take any pills. Far as I know, I don't have any medical problems like that thyroid thing you mentioned. I've just always been this way.
